marc: Quick report — our Windows async onboarding sample is tripping up a few users on 3.9-3.12. Sync example works; async raises a ConnectionError that, after digging, is an ssl.SSLCertVerificationError buried inside.

jen: Oof. Are they on conda, MS Store, or python.org? The cert lookup can differ.

marc: A mix. One is conda on Win10, another python.org on Win11. Both have certifi installed.

oscar: Common pattern: requests honors REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, but httpx/anyio async path doesn't always pick that up. Also Windows Proactor loop sometimes exposes tls/socket combos.

jen: Can you repro locally? Short workaround is to build an SSLContext using certifi and pass it into the AsyncClient, and (optionally) set the selector loop on Windows: ````python
import ssl, certifi, asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
try:
    asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())
except AttributeError:
    pass

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(ssl=ctx) as c:
        await c.generate("hi")

asyncio.run(main())
````

oscar: Two follow-ups: 1) our AsyncClient typing doesn't expose `ssl` (or `verify`) so mypy users try the wrong kwarg; 2) our retry layer strips the original __cause__ so support only sees ConnectionError.

marc: I opened issue 2701 to track typing + retry chaining + sample updates. devex-bot: created issue 2701.

devex-bot: Issue 2701 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/2701

jen: Proposed quick fixes: add Optional[ssl.SSLContext] and Optional[Union[bool,str]] verify to AsyncClient signature/stubs, preserve exception.__cause__ in retry middleware, add a small helper like `redwood.windows_ssl_context()` that returns `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())`, and document the selector-loop tip.

oscar: Also recommend a minimal Windows CI job for py3.8-3.12 (smoke test) to catch regressions. Platform flagged a lightweight matrix as OK.

marc: Thanks — that should make onboarding less painful. If anyone still sees verify failures after the changes, paste the full exception.__cause__, python build (store vs installer vs conda) and we'll follow up with a minimal repro. :thumbsup:
